question: Give reason for the following: Nitrobenzene does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation.
option1: The strongly electron-withdrawing -NO₂ group deactivates the ring toward electrophilic attack and also complexes with/deactivates the AlCl₃ Lewis acid catalyst, preventing the Friedel-Crafts reaction from proceeding
option2: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons via resonance, making the ring highly electron-deficient. Consequently, nitrobenzene preferentially undergoes nucleophilic aromatic substitution rather than electrophilic substitution, so the alkyl carbocation cannot attack the ring.
option3: The –NO₂ group severely destabilizes the Wheland intermediate (sigma complex) during electrophilic attack. Although AlCl₃ is a strong Lewis acid, the activation energy for the alkylation becomes prohibitively high due to steric hindrance from the bulky nitro group at all ring positions.
option4: AlCl₃ preferentially coordinates with the oxygen atoms of the –NO₂ group, forming a stable complex that precipitates out of the reaction mixture. Because the catalyst is removed from the system, the ring remains electron-rich but lacks the necessary Lewis acid to generate the electrophile.
correct_option: The strongly electron-withdrawing -NO₂ group deactivates the ring toward electrophilic attack and also complexes with/deactivates the AlCl₃ Lewis acid catalyst, preventing the Friedel-Crafts reaction from proceeding
